body.heading: Your environment is always suggesting something
paragraphs: The biscuit tin on the counter suggests biscuits. The book on the pillow suggests reading. Most of the time we do not choose between options after careful thought — we drift towards whatever is closest, easiest and most visible.
This is not a weakness. It is simply how attention and energy work, and it means a small rearrangement can do more than a large amount of willpower.

body.heading: Move things closer or further away
paragraphs: For a habit you want, remove a step. Lay out the walking shoes by the door. Put the guitar on a stand instead of in its case. Keep a glass of water where you work so drinking it needs no trip to the kitchen.

For a habit you want less of, add a step. Put the phone to charge in another room. Keep snacks in a tin, in a cupboard, instead of in a bowl in plain sight. Even twenty seconds of extra effort is often enough to let the urge pass.

body.heading: Change one thing at a time
paragraphs: Pick the single most annoying friction in a habit you care about and fix only that. Then live with it for a week and notice what changes.
Environment design is never finished, because your life keeps changing. Treat it as gentle tinkering rather than a one-time overhaul, and it stays enjoyable instead of becoming another chore.

takeaway: Do not fight your surroundings — rearrange them, one small thing at a time.
